analysis.investment_thesis: Anand Rathi is a high-quality wealth manager riding India's HNI/UHNI boom with exceptional ROE (47%) and near-zero debt — exactly the kind of niche dominator I love. But a trailing PEG of ~2.4x (P/E 77 / ~32% profit CAGR) and forward PEG ~1.9x price perfection into this wonderful story, leaving little margin of safety.
key_strengths: Exceptional capital efficiency: ROE 47%, ROCE 59%, operating margins 40%+ — this is a capital-light compounder
Consistent profit CAGR of 31.6% over 7 years with 5/5 positive OCF years and near-zero debt (D/E 0.08)
India's rising affluent class is a secular tailwind visible from street-level observation — this story has years to run
key_risks: PEG >2 means any growth wobble or market downturn will compress this multiple brutally — expensive stocks punish surprises
Highly market-linked revenues: a prolonged equity bear market or MF industry fee compression would hit AUM and margins hard
2026 'Other Income' surged to INR 105 Cr vs ~1 Cr historically — the real operating profit growth (INR 441→482 Cr) was more modest; headline EPS may be flattered
red_flags: Forward PEG ~1.9x — well above my 1.0x comfort zone and breaching my 1.5x hard ceiling
Operating income growth decelerated noticeably in FY26: +9% vs 33%+ in prior years, even as Other Income inflated reported profits
Promoter holding at 43% is moderate; no insider buying signal to validate the valuation
analysis.detailed_analysis: Anand Rathi Wealth is a textbook fast grower — a niche wealth manager serving HNIs/UHNIs with a sticky, fee-based model and an Omni platform for IFAs. Revenue has grown at 22% and net profit at 32% CAGR over seven years, the balance sheet is pristine (D/E 0.08), and margins are expanding. This is exactly the kind of story I want to own for the next decade as India's affluent population multiplies. The problem is price: at P/E 77x with a forward P/E of 52x, the market has already capitalised a decade of growth. My PEG discipline flags this loudly — even on a generous 30% forward growth assumption, you're paying 1.7-1.9x PEG. I hold great businesses at fair prices, not at prices that assume everything goes perfectly. Wait for a meaningful correction to the INR 2,800-3,000 range where PEG approaches 1.0x before adding aggressively.
